Mineralized skarn is denser and more chargeable than the host rocks:

laboratory testing of 18 drill core samples from Cerro Grande returned an average density of 3.76 g/cm³ for mineralized skarn, compared with averages of 2.92 g/cm³ or less for the host rocks tested, and chargeabilities of 74 to 128 ms, compared with 3 to 8 ms for unmineralized skarn.
Ground gravity survey to begin October 22, 2026:
approximately 1,296 stations across Mezquital, Cerro Grande, Cerro Potrero and Las Trancas, with the results to be integrated with the Company's magnetic, IP/MT, petrophysical and drilling data.
Gravity and IP to test existing targets and generate new ones:

more than ten structural intersections along the 7-kilometre corridor show magnetic signatures comparable to the Cerro Grande skarn; the combined gravity and IP data are designed to test these targets and may identify new ones.
Hole AG-CG-PH2-003:
intersected fault-hosted skarn at a target separate from Cerro Grande, with visible copper sulfides logged from 624.45 to 634.50 m; assays pending.
